title: Which choice gives one hundred twenty six squared?
description: The video finds one hundred twenty six squared from one hundred twenty five squared and picks the matching choice. It then puts the answer back into the question to check it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the next square is the old square plus the next odd number, and the nth odd number is two times n minus one. Watch for students who add the new side length or add two times the new side plus one.

video_script.why: The child applies the next odd number method of the solved example to pick the right choice for 126².
video_script.substitution: Find the next odd number as two times the position minus one, and add it to the known square.
video_script.anchor: the line 125² = 15625 and the five choices for 126² in a row
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred twenty six squared is fifteen thousand eight hundred seventy six

final_answer.spoken: one hundred twenty six squared is fifteen thousand eight hundred seventy six

never_show: the answer before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: the next square adds the next odd number. The five choices stay in the anchor band and the matching one is ticked at the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the line 125² = 15625 in the anchor band, and five choices for 126²: (i) 15625 + 126, (ii) 15625 + 26², (iii) 15625 + 253, (iv) 15625 + 251, (v) 15625 + 512

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='given'/>We know that one hundred twenty five squared is fifteen thousand six hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Each choice adds a number to fifteen thousand six hundred twenty five. Which choice gives one hundred twenty six squared?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and the five choices glow

marks.stop: the five choices glow in the accent colour

beats.on_screen: 8² = 64 and 9² = 81; the jump 81 − 64 = 17 is the 9th odd number, 2 × 9 − 1

marks.jump: the jump of 17 between them lights up and joins to 2 × 9 − 1

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Use the same method as for thirty six squared.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Eight squared is sixty four, and nine squared is eighty one.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>The jump is seventeen. That is the ninth odd number, which is two times nine, take away one.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one hundred twenty five squared is fifteen thousand six hundred twenty five.

beats.on_screen: To find: 126², and the matching choice

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find one hundred twenty six squared, and pick the matching choice.

marks.next: the line next square = old square + next odd number appears
marks.plus: 126² is written as 125² plus the 126th odd number

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step one, the next square adds the next odd number.
<bookmark mark='plus'/>We add the one hundred twenty sixth odd number to one hundred twenty five squared.
<bookmark mark='double'/>Step two, double one hundred twenty six to get two hundred fifty two.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Take away one, and the odd number is two hundred fifty one.

marks.match: choice (iv) is lined up beside the sum

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add two hundred fifty one to fifteen thousand six hundred twenty five. That gives fifteen thousand eight hundred seventy six.
<bookmark mark='match'/>The matching choice adds two hundred fifty one.

marks.sum: the two parts are added to 15876

narration: <bookmark mark='hundred'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. One hundred times one hundred twenty six is twelve thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='twentysix'/>Twenty six times one hundred twenty six is three thousand two hundred seventy six.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The two parts add up to fifteen thousand eight hundred seventy six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>One hundred twenty six squared is fifteen thousand eight hundred seventy six. That is choice four.
